title: One Record, Many Facts
content:
What problem does this solve?
Lists are excellent when order and position matter. A record such as one expedition has different named facts: destination, party, supplies, guide status, and clearance. A dictionary stores values under meaningful keys instead of numeric positions.

Start with the behavior
  record = {"destination": "Gloamfen", "members": 3}
  print(record["destination"])
The key "destination" names the field. Square brackets retrieve the value associated with that key.

Update and add fields
  record["status"] = "ready"
The same assignment shape can replace an existing value or add a new key.

Dictionary values can be collections
A value may itself be a list, so one record can contain a party or supply list without introducing nested dictionaries yet.

Vocabulary after the behavior
A dictionary stores key-value pairs. The key is the label used for lookup; the value is the data associated with that label.
concepts: String keys provide meaningful labels for record fields
Assignment to record[key] updates or adds a field

examples.title: Read named fields
examples.explanation: The fields are retrieved by labels rather than positions.

examples.title: Add a status
examples.explanation: Assignment adds the new named field.

examples.title: List-valued field
examples.explanation: The dictionary field can hold a list learned earlier.

common_mistakes: Writing record[destination] when the key should be the string "destination"
Using parentheses instead of square brackets for lookup
Using = instead of : inside a dictionary literal
Treating dictionary fields as numeric positions
Expecting duplicate keys to preserve multiple separate values

exercises.title: Read the record
hints: Read each key inside square brackets.
destination maps to Gloamfen and members maps to 3.
The lines are Gloamfen and 3.

exercises.title: Read one field
exercises.prompt: Change the key inside the lookup so the program prints 7.
hints: Look at the exact key stored in the dictionary literal.
Keys used for lookup must match, including quotes and spelling.
Use stats["health"].

exercises.title: Update a field
exercises.prompt: Change record["status"] from "waiting" to "ready", then print the dictionary.
exercises.starter_code:
record = {"status": "waiting"}

# Update the status, then print record
hints: Use the same square-bracket key lookup on the left side of an assignment.
Assign the new string "ready" to record["status"].
Use record["status"] = "ready", then print(record).

exercises.title: List or dictionary?
exercises.prompt: Which structure better represents one expedition with named facts such as destination, guide status, and clearance?
choices: A list, because each fact should be remembered by numeric position
A dictionary, because each fact has a meaningful label
hints: Ask whether the field names themselves are important to the model.
A reader should be able to ask for destination by name rather than remember that it is position 0.
Choose a dictionary.
exercises.success_message: Correct. The labels are part of the data model, so keys make the record clearer.

exercises.title: Quote the key
exercises.prompt: This raises NameError because Python treats destination as a variable name. Repair only the lookup.
hints: The dictionary contains a string key.
A string key must be written in quotes during lookup.
Use record["destination"].

exercises.title: Create a field record
exercises.prompt: Using the supplied destination, party, and supplies variables, create a dictionary named record with exactly these keys: destination, party, supplies, member_count. Calculate member_count with len(party), then print record.
exercises.starter_code:
destination = "Gloamfen"
party = ["Mara", "Tovin"]
supplies = ["rope"]

# Build record, then print it
exercises.reference_solution:
destination = "Gloamfen"
party = ["Mara", "Tovin"]
supplies = ["rope"]
record = {
    "destination": destination,
    "party": party,
    "supplies": supplies,
    "member_count": len(party),
}
print(record)
hints: Use the variable names as values in the dictionary; the field labels themselves are strings.
The member_count field should calculate len(party) rather than repeat the number 2.
Build record = {"destination": destination, "party": party, "supplies": supplies, "member_count": len(party)} and print it.
exercises.success_message: The expedition facts now live in one record whose fields explain themselves.

exercises.title: Expedition Intake System v1
exercises.prompt:
Build a dictionary named expedition from the supplied variables.

Preserve these fields: destination, party, supplies, has_guide, warning_active.
Add:
- member_count = len(party)
- supply_count = len(supplies)
- status = Denied if there is no guide OR a warning is active; otherwise Cleared for 5 or more supplies; otherwise Review

Print the completed dictionary. After it passes, manually test a no-guide case, warning case, 4-supply case, and exact 5-supply boundary. No multi-parameter function is required yet.
exercises.starter_code:
destination = "Gloamfen"
party = ["Mara", "Tovin"]
supplies = ["rope", "torch", "map", "chalk", "antidote"]
has_guide = True
warning_active = False

# Build and complete expedition
exercises.reference_solution:
destination = "Gloamfen"
party = ["Mara", "Tovin"]
supplies = ["rope", "torch", "map", "chalk", "antidote"]
has_guide = True
warning_active = False

expedition = {
    "destination": destination,
    "party": party,
    "supplies": supplies,
    "has_guide": has_guide,
    "warning_active": warning_active,
}
expedition["member_count"] = len(party)
expedition["supply_count"] = len(supplies)
if not has_guide or warning_active:
    expedition["status"] = "Denied"
elif len(supplies) >= 5:
    expedition["status"] = "Cleared"
else:
    expedition["status"] = "Review"
print(expedition)
hints: Build the basic dictionary first, then add the calculated fields and status one step at a time.
Handle denial first with not has_guide or warning_active. Only if that is false should supplies determine Cleared versus Review.
Create expedition from the five inputs, add member_count and supply_count with len, then use if not has_guide or warning_active / elif len(supplies) >= 5 / else to assign expedition["status"].
exercises.success_message: Checkpoint complete: the intake system now combines named data, calculated fields, Boolean blockers, and threshold decisions.
